pairs.subject: audit-logging
pairs.evidence: lib/ledger/v1/sources/clips.ts:91 Adapters copy vendor error strings (clips, extract, forge, mv) and whole v1 log lines (extract.ts:150) verbatim into the data of an append-only, hash-chained ledger, with no allowlist, size cap or redaction. Any credential or oversized text in a vendor message is archived for good, against write-path-sanitization.

techniques.evidence: lib/ledger/v1/sources/clips.ts:91 Free-form vendor error goes in uncapped and unscrubbed. The same pattern appears in extract.ts:156, forge.ts:130 and mv.ts:122.

lib/ledger/v1/sources/sound.ts:74 The v1 instant is passed as the effective time. The earlier deviation is not upheld: a null judgedAt becomes atSrc 'derived', which the store keeps and the Ledger renders as '≈'. The defaulted rows stay distinguishable, which the named failure mode says they are not.
lib/ledger/v1/sources/sound.ts:62 A re-verdict is keyed as a new fact rather than overwriting the old one, so the trail keeps kept→rejected→kept.
lib/ledger/v1/sources/clips.ts:78 An unreadable record is counted with its reason (it becomes an ingest.skip fact), never silently dropped.

pairs.subject: audit-logging
pairs.evidence: lib/ledger/v1/facts.ts:102 The shared fact builder, which every adapter goes through, copies each v1 log line whole into event data, and nothing between it and appendOnce applies an allowlist, size cap or secret scrub. The ledger, append-only and hash-chained, archives whatever a log line held, against write-path-sanitization.

techniques.evidence: lib/ledger/v1/facts.ts:102 No cap or redaction at the projection's chokepoint. The kernel's eventDataSchema accepts any JSON.

lib/ledger/v1/facts.ts:92 Effective time is kept apart from the kernel's recorded `at`. An unknown instant is labelled 'derived' and keeps the raw text. Nuance: line 90 still fills occurredAt with the sync time rather than leaving it absent. That is distinguishable through atSrc, so it is not the named unrecoverable failure, which is why the earlier deviation is not upheld.
lib/ledger/v1/sync.ts:36 Failures are classed, recorded as ingest.fail events and counted in a per-source streak table.
lib/ledger/v1/sync.ts:133 Every projected event enters through a single appendOnce door, in batches.
lib/ledger/v1/sync.ts:68 A changed key is counted as drift, never rewritten in place.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/read.ts:15 Pages report capped/scanned/exhausted. The empty result says '0 in the newest N' (List.tsx:125) rather than claiming none. Reads are gated by principal('read') (actions.ts:31). Reads are not themselves recorded, which is defensible for a single-operator studio.
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/actions.ts:3 The screen exports only reads; there is no edit or delete path to the trail.

app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/vocab.ts:95 The detail shows the recorded clock beside the effective time, with a 'time derived ≈' / 'time recorded' chip (Detail.tsx:122). The window is documented as on `t` (filter.ts:192).
app/(studio)/ledger/page.tsx:46 A failed sync is surfaced on the query surface itself, not only in a log.
packages/kernel/src/events.ts:77 Events are never invalidated, so there is no record-axis interval to rewind (the technique's own exemption).
packages/kernel/src/events.ts:50 Nothing has been retired from the event ledger yet, so there is no horizon notice the query surface owes.
